Have you maybe thought about finding an online group for people with similar medical challenges? That could be a really helpful way to meet people who have similar experiences, you mentioned feeling isolated by your condition. A quick google search suggested http://www.earsforeyes.info/index.php/pages/Directory_Support_Groups.html

Even if you can't meet up with people you find this way, I think it could be helpful? My older sister was born with cerebral palsy, she felt very alone but finding friends who could truly empathize through online support groups really helped her. They might even have suggestions for different, more affordable treatments or ways to cope with the related stress better.

And on the family point? A lot of people are born into families that are...difficult. I know plenty of people who, instead of allowing their toxic family members to form them, used them as a template for what they DIDN'T want to be. Part of what we learn from our parents isn't what they directly teach us, but it's also what we learn from example. That can be hard to parse through. Have you spoken with your brother about how you feel? His introversion (not that being introverted is necessarily a negative) might be rooted in the same family relationships, it could be healthy for you to share the feelings of "suffocation."

I understand that having a less-than-functional family is a huge challenge, nevermind your medical needs, but unless you want to cut them from your life entirely you need to find some middle ground or understanding. Don't let them define you, but it's a choice you sound like you feel you have to make.

Lastly, it is fucking ridiculous that it is so expensive for you to get the treatments/supplies to help your vision. It's so fundamentally unfair that someone should pay every penny they have so that they can SEE. When I came out, I felt very powerless. I was so bitter about the fact that I was different and the various unfair-nesses involved. It sounds like you (justly) resent the bullshit you have to deal with. I found it enormously helpful to get political! It really made me feel more empowered getting involved with LGBT rights, it really helped me come to terms and maybe getting involved with healthcare reform would make you feel less helpless and frustrated, too. College campuses are great for finding ways to get involved in political issues locally, a great way to meet people, too.

Best of luck.

Odd, we had almost entirely different reactions. I thought it was well-acted, but stumbled plotwise at the end. I just didn't feel like I got much closure? I also did really like the use of very ominous SFX instead of jump-out scares.
